title: You Framed My Rams
logline: The zun notices the visitor photographing its flawless-looking ram head and tells them that this same vessel was destroyed by bomb attacks during the war.
voice: A man in his sixties, low grainy baritone, neutral English, slow, quietly amused.
narrator_attitude: Fond and a little wry toward the visitor who just photographed its rams. It is pleased to be admired, but it gently corrects the idea that it was never broken.
music_style: Sparse slow struck bronze bells, long metallic decay.
subject_lock: Dark grey-green bronze square zun, flared square mouth with tall hooked flanges, four ram foreparts with spiralling curled horns at the corners, fine scale and spiral patterns, high square foot.
living_form_lock: The same square zun freshly cast: polished golden-brown bronze, flared square mouth with tall hooked flanges, four ram foreparts with spiralling curled horns at the corners, crisp scale and spiral patterns, high square foot.

narration.text: You photographed my rams as if untouched.
In nineteen thirty-eight, a Hunan hillside gave me up.
Look up. During the war, bombs destroyed me.
